title: The Unsaid Undertow
premise: Casper Blackwood, a night librarian in a sleepless coastal city, discovers a box of undelivered letters hidden behind a wardrobe in the condemned house where he grew up — letters his mother wrote to a man who died the night Casper survived and never spoke of it again. As demolition approaches, he traces the letters' intended recipient, uncovering that his father's death was no accident and that his mother's silence was bought with fear. The story ends with Casper delivering the final letter himself, choosing truth over the protective quiet that has defined his life, even though it costs him the last person who still loves him.
about_author: Odile Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters in municipal storage. She writes at night, in cities that refuse to sleep.

chapters.title: The Hours Between
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the library's dead hours, Casper tends to insomniacs and shelved griefs, establishing his ritualized avoidance of feeling. A demolition notice for his childhood street arrives in returned mail. Emotional beat: the numb comfort of routine about to be broken.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: POV Casper. He breaks into the condemned family house to retrieve one photograph and finds a cavity behind the wardrobe stuffed with unsent letters, all addressed to a name he doesn't recognize: Elias Vann. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past is not where he left it.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: POV Casper, with letters in italicized second voice. Reading the letters, he learns his mother loved another man during the year before his father drowned. The final letter is dated three days after the drowning and is never finished. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Casper. He tracks Elias Vann through harbor records and finds he vanished from the city the week after the death — alive, then erased. An old dockworker lets slip that people were paid to forget. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into dread.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: POV Mara, Casper's estranged sister, a defense lawyer who chose duty over family. She remembers their mother's fear differently — the locked doors, the hush money. She warns Casper to stop digging. Emotional beat: love expressed as obstruction; two survivors, opposite strategies.

chapters.title: The Drowned Year
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Flashbacks surface: twelve-year-old Casper saw something on the pier the night his father died and was made to promise silence. He realizes the letters weren't hidden from him — they were hidden because of what he witnessed. Emotional beat: the price of survival revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: POV Elias Vann, now dying in a coastal town upriver. He receives Casper's call and confesses: he didn't kill the father, but he watched men do it and ran, taking the mother's letters as his only proof she ever forgave him. Emotional beat: guilt meeting its mirror.

chapters.title: Demolition Eve
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The men paid to forget learn Casper has the letters. Mara must choose between protecting her brother and protecting her career; she tips off the police instead of the family's old paymasters. Emotional beat: duty finally bending toward love.

chapters.title: The Undertow
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Confrontation at the house on demolition morning: the man who arranged the drowning comes for the letters, and Casper finally speaks aloud what he saw at twelve — breaking the promise that structured his whole life. Emotional beat: climax; speech as survival, survival as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Delivered
chapters.summary: POV Casper, coda. The house falls; the truth enters the record. Casper hand-delivers his mother's unfinished letter to Elias, adding a line of his own to finish it. Mara stands beside him, imperfectly reconciled. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — the unsaid, at last, said.
